edges.description: Loss of the a1 proton-pumping subunit raises endolysosomal pH.
Without an acidic lumen, lysosomal hydrolysis and autophagosome turnover fail.
Degradative failure in neurons drives neurodegeneration, prominent in the cerebellum in the recessive arm.
Neuronal dysfunction produces the progressive myoclonus epilepsy.
Neuronal degradative failure underlies the intellectual disability.

nodes.description: Reduced V-ATPase activity fails to acidify the endolysosomal compartment. Overexpression of two biallelic (recessive-arm) alleles, A512P and N534D, impairs lysosomal acidification in neuronal cells, giving the recessive arm direct functional evidence of the acidification defect; a recurrent de novo allele (R740Q) shows the same defect.
